title: The Scale of Plunder and Slaughter in Delhi

blocks.text: This page sums up the devastation left by the invasion in stark, collective terms. The poet says that wealth beyond counting was carried off from the Mughal dominions and that the destruction of Delhi exposed the fragility of a court that had imagined itself unassailable.

Human loss is counted alongside treasure. The narrative highlights that seventy thousand killed in Delhi were largely defenseless people, making the catastrophe a moral indictment of imperial failure rather than a mere change of rulers.

The conclusion is that the Mughals had effectively ruined themselves through their own corruption and violence. That judgment prepares the reader for the next episode, where the Khalsa’s suffering is again placed before the divine court and answered through history.
